title: Diatonic Passing Tones: Descend & Ascend
subtitle: Ten favourite concert keys · full written alto range
tonal: Choose 1 of 10 concert keys → automatically written for E♭ alto
progression: A single major or natural-minor scale, transposed to written alto. The note pattern follows the key; no chromatic outside notes.
goal: Build fluent, even finger motion through overlapping descending three-note scale groups, then reverse direction at the lowest available scale tone and climb to the highest again.
palette: Ten concert keys in favourite order: B minor / D major; F♯ minor / A major; A minor / C major; B♭ minor / D♭ major; E minor / G major. Written E♭ alto transposition appears in Play.
saxChords: No chord changes. Follow the selected written major or natural-minor scale. Every three-note group contains two adjacent scale steps: e.g. written C major F–(E)–D, E–(D)–C, D–(C)–B.
backing: A steady 4/4 drum groove, with adjustable tempo and note-change rate using Sax Play's existing drums. Fingering pictures appear one note at a time. No lead instrument or new audio required.
steps: 2 MIN · CHOOSE YOUR KEY Select one of the ten concert keys in Sax Play; read the corresponding written alto key before starting.
5 MIN · DESCEND Start on the highest written sax note that belongs to that scale. Play overlapping three-note groups: top–middle–bottom, then move the starting note down one scale step.
5 MIN · ASCEND At the lowest complete three-note group, reverse: bottom–middle–top, then shift the starting note up one scale step until you return to the highest note.
5 MIN · EVENNESS Repeat with the same air support and relaxed fingers. Move gradually from a comfortable note-change rate to a quicker one without rushing the crossing of the octave key.
3 MIN · REVIEW Note one awkward transition or register break. Repeat just that passage before another full down-and-up run.
bringHome: One smooth descent and ascent in a chosen key, with accurate fingering and even tone through the registers.
extension: Choose a second favourite key, or repeat the same key with contrasting articulation. Keep all passing notes inside its diatonic scale.
